tip: куда (kuda = where to) asks about direction and pairs with motion verbs like ведёт (vedyot = leads).
купил (kupil) is perfective, a finished one-time buy; imperfective покупал (pakupal) would mean was buying or used to buy.
какое (kakoe = what a) is neuter, matching здание (zdanie = building). красивое (krasivaye) agrees in neuter too; a masculine noun would take какой (kakoy).
бегает (begaet = runs) is the habitual form for repeated action, fitting каждое утро (kazhdaye utra = every morning). One run in progress would be бежит (bezhit).
два (dva = two) takes genitive singular: два года (dva goda = two years), not the plural годы (gody). Numbers 2, 3, 4 all do this.
один (adin = one) keeps the noun nominative singular: двадцать один год (dvadtsat adin god = twenty-one years), not года (goda). Numbers ending in 1 usually do this.
сколько (skolka = how much) takes genitive: сколько времени (skolka vremeni = how much time). The base время (vremya) shifts to времени.
музыку (muzyku = music) is the object form of музыка (muzyka). Most feminine nouns change their ending when they are the direct object.
хорошего вечера (kharosheva vechera = good evening) uses genitive: good wishes are stated in the genitive, literally 'of a good evening', not nominative.
размер обуви (razmer obuvi = shoe size): the second noun goes genitive to mean 'size of footwear'. Base обувь (obuv) becomes обуви.
с (s = with) takes instrumental: с твоей машиной (s tvayey mashinay = with your car). Base машина (mashina) becomes машиной.
чей (chey = whose) is masculine to match зонтик (zontik = umbrella). A feminine noun would take чья (chya) instead.
даже если (dazhe esli = even if) introduces a concession: даже если болеет (baleyet = is sick), he still works.
свои (svoi = one's own) points back to the subject and matches the thing owned: свои мечты (svoi mechty = one's own dreams).
мне (mne = to me) is dative: age is stated with dative, literally 'to me thirty-two years', not with я (ya = I).
помочь (pamoch = to help) takes dative with no word for 'to': помочь вам (pamoch vam = help you). вам is the dative of вы (vy = you).
умеет (umeet) means know how to, a learned skill, not passing ability. не умеет плавать (ne umeet plavat) = never learned to swim.
Neuter subjects take было in the past: задание было (zadanie bylo = the assignment was); masculine был (byl), feminine была (byla).
Russian gives age with the person in the dative, not the nominative; ему (yemu = to him) is that dative, meaning he is the one who is twenty-five.
нравится (nravitsya = is pleasing) puts the liker in the dative; мне (mne = to me) is that dative, so the line reads the movie does not please me.
по (po) plus the dative marks a repeated occasion. по выходным (po vykhadnym) = on weekends, meaning every weekend, not a single one.
нет (net = there is no) forces the genitive on the missing thing. нет времени (net vremeni = no time) uses the genitive, not the nominative.
стоит (stoit = is worth) with a dative person gives soft advice; тебе (tebe = to you) не стоит (ne stoit) means you would be better off not doing it.
Seasons take the instrumental to mean in that season. осенью (osen'yu = in autumn) needs no preposition, the ending alone carries in.
пахнет (pakhnet = smells) takes the instrumental for the scent. свежей выпечкой (svezhey vypechkay) = of fresh baking, with no separate word for of.
Numbers five and above usually take a genitive plural noun. пять учеников (pyat uchenikov = students) uses the genitive plural, not the plain plural.
Negation stacks in Russian: никогда (nikagda = never) still needs не (ne) before the verb, никогда не были (nikagda ne byli = have never been).
могли бы (magli by) is the polite could you. The particle бы (by) is what softens a request into would you mind.
меня зовут (menya zavut = me they call) is the standard way to give your name. меня (menya) is the object, so there is no word for I.
назад (nazad = ago) comes after the time span: две недели назад (dve nedeli nazad = two weeks ago), never before it.
